title: Integral scalar extension respects signed biduality and finite Hom reductions
statement: Fix D,l,E⊂L,X,wE,wL and the canonical maps of [def-sf-integral-finite-extension-core]. For normalized source/target tensor presentations a,b, their signed Koszul symmetries sE,sL and normalized quotient presentations mE,mL [def-sf-integral-hom-reduction-models; def-sf-integral-verdier-models], assume both swaps are natural and that the evaluations of a, b and of every finite target presentation of mE, mL are natural in the first tensor variable. Then scalar extension commutes with the actual signed double-dual morphism via beta, with the finite evaluation-defined internal-Hom comparison via v, and with the finite Verdier comparison via beta. The finite equations use exactly quotient, homMap and finiteU, at every exponent n+1 including intervening ramified levels. Inputs are integral bounded constructible; no invertibility or identity/composition conclusion is included.

source.place: Paragraphs 5-7: transpose scalar evaluation, the double-dual square and finite quotient equations.

proof.text: Use simultaneous signed tensor-Hom models and their normalized evaluations. The scalar tensorator multiplies degree-zero coefficient factors and therefore commutes with the Koszul swap. Transpose scalar evaluation in each input; the two double-dual composites have the same transpose, giving the actual delta square.

Tensor the same evaluation representative with every finite quotient. Tensor balancing identifies its transpose with the finite homMap conjugated by quotient. This is the v equation; no freeness of the intervening quotient is needed. Postcompose with finiteU and use u_reduction and Hom naturality to obtain the beta equation. Simultaneous localization preserves these equations, so no faithfulness claim for separate finite evaluations is used.
